subject: Business Models
title: Cars as a Subscription
description: A short lesson to help you apply Cars as a Subscription.

hook.text: BMW tried to charge $18/month to use your car's heated seats. They were already installed in the car.

buildup.text: Automakers are exploring subscriptions for features: heated seats, faster acceleration, self-driving modes.

discovery.text: Tesla charges $199/month for 'Full Self-Driving.' The hardware is in every car; software unlocks it.

twist.text: BMW reversed its heated seat subscription after massive backlash. Some features feel wrong behind a paywall.

climax.text: Cars may become subscription platforms: pay monthly to unlock features in a product you already own.

punchline.text: Buy the car, subscribe to the features. Ownership is being redefined.

quiz.question: Why did BMW reverse its heated seat subscription?

details.summary: Car subscriptions offer monthly access to vehicles including insurance, maintenance, and the ability to switch cars, replacing traditional ownership and leasing. Volvo Care, Porsche Drive, and various startups charge monthly premiums that eliminate the complexities of car ownership.
details.whyItMatters: Car subscriptions represent the access-over-ownership trend reaching one of the most expensive consumer purchases. If successful at scale, they could disrupt auto financing, insurance, and dealership models that generate trillions in annual revenue.
takeaways: Monthly all-inclusive fees replace purchase, financing, and insurance
Subscribers can swap vehicles to match changing needs or preferences
Premium pricing currently limits adoption to higher-income consumers

faq.question: How do car subscriptions differ from traditional leases?
faq.answer: Subscriptions include insurance, maintenance, and roadside assistance in one monthly payment. Most allow car swaps within the fleet. Terms are flexible with monthly cancellation options. Leases require separate insurance, have fixed terms, and do not allow vehicle changes.

faq.question: Why have car subscription services struggled to scale?
faq.answer: High vehicle costs require premium monthly pricing of $500+. Depreciation and maintenance create thin margins. Insurance costs are unpredictable. Utilization rates must stay high to cover fleet capital costs. Most services target luxury segments where pricing is less sensitive.
